transcript:
Meeting header: 2025-12-02 10:00 PST | Duration: 45m | Attendees: Alyssa, Marco, Jordan (Redwood); Priya, Liam, Sofia, Ankit (CityFin)

Summary (auto): Quick review of week over week quality; one regression noted on the customer support prompt; agreed next steps to run dedicated benchmarks and tighten guardrails.

00:00 Speaker 1 (Alyssa): hey everyone, thanks for joining, uh quick check, can you all see my screen?
00:05 Speaker 2 (Priya): yep seeing it, thanks Alyssa.
00:12 Speaker 1 (Alyssa): cool — agenda, we'll run through the eval sheet, highlight any regressions, then talk guardrails and a short plan for dedicated run if needed. Marco will share the numbers.
00:25 Speaker 3 (Marco): hey all, i've got the week over week table up. We ran the same 420-case prompt set, the aggregated BLEU-ish style score we use is up 0.6% across the board, but there's a localized drop on the "support-summary" prompt by about 4.2%.
00:40 Speaker 2 (Priya): 4.2, ouch. is that from a model change or prompt drift?
00:48 Speaker 3 (Marco): so, we checked, it's not a backend model version change on our hosted side; looks like a combination — one of the new paraphrase templates in the prompt set increased variance. Some answer truncation as well under long context.
01:05 Speaker 4 (Liam): yeah i saw that in our logs, the KV cache had a couple of misses; some of the longer tickets are getting cut. Could that be sequence length handling?
01:15 Speaker 3 (Marco): possibly — on hosted we have a shorter prefix preservation to keep latency low. If we switch to dedicated with slightly larger context allocation or different kernel selection, the truncation goes away but cost per token increases.
01:30 Speaker 1 (Alyssa): that's the classic latency vs cost tradeoff. Priya, what's the success criteria you set again for the POC?
01:37 Speaker 2 (Priya): primary is >=92% pass rate on the high-priority prompt set and median latency under 350ms for 95th pct — that's what product needs.
01:50 Speaker 3 (Marco): noted — current median 95th is around 380ms on hosted for the real-world set, so we need to tighten that. Dedicated gave us 320ms in the baseline test but with a 12% higher cost.
02:05 Speaker 5 (Sofia): can you clarify the cost delta? we're trying to prep numbers for the execs.
02:12 Speaker 3 (Marco): rough back-of-envelope: hosted at current QPS and caching patterns is about $0.018 per user request equivalent; dedicated optimized for latency is ~$0.020 per request, so ~12%. Numbers will vary with batching and quantization.
02:30 Speaker 2 (Priya): okay. we can probably accept a delta if latency meets SLOs. but we need to fix the regression first.
02:38 Speaker 3 (Marco): for the regression, i dug into the prompt variants — one guardrail rule (the entity redaction step) is flagging more false positives when the model paraphrases. So we're seeing more redactions than needed.
02:52 Speaker 4 (Liam): that's bad, it leads to lower utility. can we tune the guardrail classifier?
02:58 Speaker 3 (Marco): yes — options: 1) loosen the redaction threshold, 2) add a secondary heuristics step, 3) run a small fine-tune / instruction-tuning pass on the in-house prompt set. Fine-tune will take time.
03:15 Speaker 6 (Ankit): from security's perspective, we prefer guardrails being conservative; false negatives are riskier, but the product team is right, too many false positives hurt UX. can we add an allowlist for certain customer ticket types?
03:30 Speaker 1 (Alyssa): good idea. Marco, can you add an allowlist and also surface an examples list for manual review?
03:37 Speaker 3 (Marco): yep — i'll add a short allowlist that exempts known safe entities from redaction and we'll log examples for review.
03:45 Speaker 5 (Sofia): another thing — our scoring rubric seems to weight semantic correctness higher than formatting; for support summaries we care about conciseness, maybe we need to adjust weights.
03:56 Speaker 3 (Marco): noted — i can produce a version of the eval sheet with an adjusted weighting (conciseness + factuality + safety).
04:05 Speaker 2 (Priya): thanks. also Liam will push five new real tickets to the prompt set this week — you'll have more realistic coverage.
04:13 Speaker 4 (Liam): yep doing that by Friday.
04:18 Speaker 3 (Marco): regarding the regression run, i'll run a 50-case regression with both hosted and dedicated configs, include KV/cache warm vs cold, and post the raw logs. expected finish EOD 2025-12-08.
04:32 Speaker 1 (Alyssa): great — on the security/compliance front, Ankit had a list of SOC2/KMS questions last time. Ankit, anything new?
04:39 Speaker 6 (Ankit): i'm pulling the KMS flow diagram; we want to confirm BYOK options and HSM support in the Private offering, and also audit log retention period. we'll send the precise questions to Alyssa by Monday.
04:52 Speaker 1 (Alyssa): we'll attach the security packet and the architecture diagram. Jordan — can you drop the SOC2 one-pager in the repo?
04:58 Speaker 7 (Jordan): yes will do after the call.
05:02 Speaker 3 (Marco): quick note on hallucination checks — one of the scoring cases returned an invented vendor name in the response; we added a hallucination flag in the rubric and that case failed. We should add more negative examples to the training set.
05:18 Speaker 2 (Priya): that's concerning; can we apply a post-filter to cross-check entity mentions against the ticket metadata?
05:25 Speaker 3 (Marco): yes — a straightforward heuristic would be to compare named entities against ticket fields; if mismatch, mark for review or run a stricter prompt. adds small latency.
05:40 Speaker 5 (Sofia): acceptable if it's only for high-priority tickets.
05:45 Speaker 3 (Marco): agreed. we'll gate stricter checks to P1/P2.
05:50 Speaker 1 (Alyssa): any competitors we should call out — Priya you mentioned Anthropic in your RFP; how much are they in play?
05:58 Speaker 2 (Priya): we're still evaluating Anthropic and OpenAI for accuracy— cost and latency are similar, but we like Redwood's observability and runbook.
06:12 Speaker 3 (Marco): to help, i'll export the per-route latency/cost table and include estimated monthly cost numbers for both hosted and dedicated.
06:20 Speaker 1 (Alyssa): ok let's recap next steps and owners.
06:26 Speaker 3 (Marco): i'll run the regression and upload results (due 2025-12-08).
06:30 Speaker 1 (Alyssa): i'll share the eval spreadsheet with prompt versioning and the guardrail config (due 2025-12-04).
06:36 Speaker 4 (Liam): i'll provide 5 real prompts from prod by 2025-12-05.
06:40 Speaker 6 (Ankit): i'll send SOC2/KMS questions by 2025-12-06.
06:46 Speaker 7 (Jordan): i'll drop the SOC2 one-pager and security packet link into the shared folder after the call.
06:52 Speaker 2 (Priya): schedule next sync? same time next week works for me.
06:56 Speaker 1 (Alyssa): same time next Tuesday, 10am PT, i'll send calendar invite.
07:00 Speaker 5 (Sofia): thanks everyone, good call.
07:03 End of call.

References: Eval spreadsheet link (shared): https://app.redwood.example/evals/cityfin-weekly-2025-12-02 (internal link), Security packet: https://redwood.example/security/cityfin-packet.pdf
